title: ASASSN-14ko flares in 2007 (SuperWASP) and 2008 (Swift) show a slow period decrease before 2016 and a temporary fast decrease in 2018-2020; earlier clocks miss them by 11-72 days
abstract: Question: the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko has been timed only since its discovery in 2014. Payne et al. (2021) stated that no earlier data constrain when its flares began; all published and campaign clocks were fitted to 2014-2026 data. Do pre-2014 archives contain flares, and what do they show about the period history? Approach: we searched Catalina (no data returned), ASAS-3 (26 valid points) and SuperWASP DR1 (9,722 points, 2006-2008), and measured the only pre-2014 Swift visits (2008 July). We made SuperWASP differential photometry, ran a matched-filter flare search on the galaxy and 20 comparison stars, fitted the flare (MCMC), timed the 2008 UV flare against seven 2020-2024 UVW2 flares, converted both events to the campaign X-ray dip clock and added them to the 2014-2026 timing set. We tested frozen clocks, fitted ten clock models to 21 points, predicted the 2007-2008 points from 2014-2026 fits, and compared a period random walk (Kalman filter). Results: SuperWASP shows a flare in 2007 December (half-rise MJD 54437.58 +/- 0.24, amplitude 5.9 % of the aperture flux, decline 21 d; search statistic 12.7 against a comparison maximum of 4.2). Swift shows a declining UV flare in 2008 July (UVW2 above 95 % of 2020-2026 visits; peak MJD 54670.4 +/- 3.4). They are two cycles apart (local period 116.0 +/- 1.7 d) and 22 and 20 cycles before the first ASAS-SN flare; other cycle counts fit worse. The Payne et al. (2022) ephemeris misses them by 62-72 d, and frozen campaign clocks by 11-60 d, including the preferred precessing-drag clock (33-39 d). The forms of the b03f0a97 clocks fail by Delta AIC 35-51 (out-of-sample: 5.5 sigma). The best clocks have a slow decrease before 2016-2018 (-0.13 d per cycle, or zero), a fast episode of -0.55 d per cycle in 2018-2020, a constant period in 2020-2023 and -0.20 d per cycle after; the 2007-2026 mean is -0.13 to -0.19 d per cycle, 35-55 % below the published Pdot. A constant Pdot plus a 2.9-d sinusoid (19.7 cycles) fits equally on the main set but not with 2014-2016 V-band flares added. A period random walk fits worse than a smooth modulation (Delta AIC 15.8); a refitted precessing-drag clock is worse by Delta AIC 12-21. Flare 41 half-rise forecast: 2026 November 8-14. Limitations: two pre-2014 points; the 48-arcsec SuperWASP aperture includes faint field sources; the 2008 peak time has a 3.4-d error; lags assumed constant; episodic and sinusoid clocks are not separable.

We extend its frozen clocks M0-M3 backward; all miss the 2007-2008 flares by 11-60 d, and the refitted precessing-drag clock is worse than the best clocks by Delta AIC 12-21.
